clips.label: Question 1
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Five-step needs analysis sequence. When beginning an audiovisual design project, what is the primary objective of conducting a formal needs analysis before selecting any equipment? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Identify the activities end users must perform and define the functional descriptions of systems supporting those activities. Option B. Lock in final equipment model numbers and dealer quotes before interviewing stakeholders. Option C. Generate point-to-point wiring schedules and rack elevations for the installation crew. Option D. Complete post-integration performance verification checklists under ANSI/AVIXA 10:2013.

clips.label: Question 3
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Open-ended stakeholder interview questions. During an initial stakeholder discovery interview, which question style is most effective for encouraging end users to explain their workflow frustrations and how they think about the space? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Closed-ended questions that ask for a single date or yes/no confirmation. Option B. Directive questions that steer the client toward a specific flat-panel brand. Option C. Open-ended questions such as asking what they would like to see done differently or better. Option D. Rhetorical questions that assume the existing system design should be duplicated.

Upward viewing increases screen gain by reflecting ceiling luminaires into the viewer cone. Option C. Seated viewers naturally look 45 degrees above horizontal when resting at a conference table. Option D. Color discrimination functions only when the viewer looks more than 35 degrees above horizontal.

clips.label: Question 10
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Population anthropometrics and seated eye height. A designer is planning sightlines for an elementary school media center and a corporate boardroom in Japan. Why is it an error to use a single North American adult average seated eye height for both rooms? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Seated eye height varies significantly by age and regional population anthropometrics, directly altering the 30-degree sightline geometry. Option B. Elementary school rooms do not require unobstructed sightlines to the bottom of the display. Option C. ANSI/AVIXA V202.01 requires all sightlines to be measured from standing eye height regardless of furniture. Option D. Seated eye height affects only loudspeaker impedance calculations and has no effect on screen mounting height.

clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Control interface accessibility for visually impaired users. During a functional needs assessment for a public university lecture hall, stakeholders emphasize that profoundly visually impaired instructors must operate the room independently. What control interface decision follows from this requirement? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Standard flat capacitive touch screens without tactile markers are rarely suitable and accessible tactile or assistive alternatives must be designed. Option B. Touch panels should simply be mounted higher than 1500 mm above the finished floor. Option C. Visual feedback icons on the glass touch screen should be changed from green to blue. Option D. All room controls should be locked inside the equipment rack with no lectern interface.

clips.label: Question 20
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Separating justified needs from unexamined wish lists. During a programming meeting, a department head requests an 8K videowall and broadcast robotics for a small internal huddle room with a modest budget. How should the AV designer handle this request? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Separate justified functional needs from wish-list items that exceed the budget and educate the client on practical trade-offs. Option B. Add every requested item to the design without checking the owner's budget allocation. Option C. Bypass the client contact and complain directly to the company's chief executive officer. Option D. Secretly substitute low-resolution consumer televisions during installation without telling the stakeholder.

clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: DCI 4K versus UHD 4K resolution distinction in client standards. A client's technology master plan asks for '4K projection' in both their cinema screening theatre and their 16:9 corporate boardrooms. What distinction must the CTS-D clarify in the standard? Choose the single best answer. Option A. DCI 4K is 4096 × 2160 (roughly 17:9 aspect ratio), whereas UHD 4K is 3840 × 2160 (16:9 aspect ratio), affecting screen sizing and EDID tables. Option B. DCI 4K uses interlaced scanning at 24 fields per second, whereas UHD 4K is analog component video. Option C. Both DCI 4K and UHD 4K have a 4:3 aspect ratio and identical horizontal pixel counts. Option D. UHD 4K requires no HDCP encryption, whereas DCI 4K runs over single-pair Cat 3 telephone wire.

Equipment rooms are required by NEC to operate at zero relative humidity.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Tiered floor and staggered seating coordination. An architect presents a flat-floor auditorium layout with aligned seating for 180 people. What combination should the AV designer recommend to lower back-row sightlines and prevent head-and-shoulder obstruction? Choose the single best answer. Option A. A sloped or tiered floor combined with staggered seating so viewers look between the shoulders of the row ahead. Option B. A flat floor with higher-backed executive swivel chairs aligned directly behind one another. Option C. Raising the projection screen against the ceiling so the front row looks up at a 60-degree angle. Option D. Reducing the aisle width to 300 mm to pack all seats closer to the stage.

Approximately 3.14 lux; the formula converts correlated color temperature into lumens.

Exactly 50:1 between adjacent tabletops and the presenter's face.

clips.label: Question 80
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Weakest-link rule and avoiding unlocked threaded pipe couplings. Why should an AV designer avoid specifying multiple threaded pipe couplings in long overhead projector suspension drops, and how is the overall assembly's Safe Working Load determined? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Each threaded coupling adds a mechanical weak point that can unscrew under vibration unless mechanically locked, and the weakest single component governs the SWL of the entire assembly. Option B. Adding more threaded couplings increases the Safe Working Load proportionally with each joint. Option C. Threaded steel pipes are only rated for horizontal conduit pulls and cannot carry vertical tension. Option D. The assembly's Safe Working Load is the average of the strongest and weakest components.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Including mounting hardware weight in the 5:1 load calculation. Why is this a critical load-calculation error? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The 5:1 safety factor must be applied to the total suspended weight—including the devices, mounting frame, brackets, adapters, and cabling—not just the bare display. Option B. Mounting frames and rigging brackets are weightless once attached to structural steel. Option C. The safety factor for mounting hardware is 1:1 while only optical lenses require 5:1. Option D. Cables and brackets push upward on the ceiling and subtract from the suspended load.

clips.label: Question 86
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Rack cooling pressurization vs evacuation methods. When coordinating equipment rack thermal management, what is the primary advantage of the pressurization cooling method (pushing filtered cool air into the bottom of the rack) over simple top-fan evacuation? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Maintaining positive air pressure inside the rack reduces dust ingress through seams and openings while driving hot air out the top vents. Option B. Pressurization forces hot air downward from the top of the rack to heat the UPS batteries at the bottom. Option C. Pressurization allows adjacent rack devices with opposite front-to-back and back-to-front airflows to cool each other without blanking panels. Option D. Pressurization eliminates the need to exhaust heat from the equipment room into the building HVAC system.

Why must the AV designer coordinate HVAC supply-air diffuser locations with the mechanical engineer in a presentation auditorium? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Option B. HVAC supply ducts must blow directly into open condenser microphones to cool their preamplifiers. Option C. Return air grilles must be sealed shut whenever the projector lamp is energized. Option D. Air diffusers increase the electrical impedance of nearby 70 V speaker lines.

Phase-to-neutral voltage is always exactly half of the phase-to-phase voltage. Option C. Phase-to-neutral voltage equals phase-to-phase voltage multiplied by 3.41. Option D. Three-phase commercial services have no neutral conductor and supply only 480 V DC.

clips.label: Question 90
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: MEP branch-circuit and heat-load coordination sequence. Arrange the steps for specifying AV electrical branch circuits and HVAC thermal loads for the MEP engineering team in the proper sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Gather rated voltage, current, power consumption, and efficiency data for every AV device under typical simultaneous use. Step 2: Group receptacles onto dedicated single-phase AV branch circuits so each circuit stays at or below its continuous current limit (e.g., 16 A on a 20 A circuit). Step 3: Calculate total room and rack heat dissipation in kJ/hr or Btu/hr, adjusting power amplifiers for actual efficiency and duty cycle. Step 4: Document circuit locations, grounding notes, harmonic neutral demands, and thermal loads on the A&E coordination drawings for the MEP engineers.

clips.label: Question 91
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Harmonic currents and double-sized neutral conductor specification. Why must an AV designer inform the electrical engineer when an installation includes a large concentration of switched-mode power supplies and phase-control lighting dimmers on a three-phase system? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. Non-linear switched-mode and dimmer loads generate third-harmonic currents that add rather than cancel in the neutral return, often requiring the neutral conductor to be sized at up to double the phase capacity. Option B. Switched-mode power supplies reduce the neutral current to zero even when only one phase is loaded. Option C. Phase-control dimmers convert AC mains power into 48 V DC phantom power on the neutral wire. Option D. Harmonic currents allow the electrician to downsize the branch-circuit overcurrent breakers by 50 percent.

Choose the single best answer. Option A. 53% for one cable, 31% for two cables, and 40% for three or more cables; a three-cable jam ratio (conduit ID ÷ cable OD) between 2.8 and 3.2 risks jamming at bends and requires the next larger conduit. Option B. 80% for one cable, 60% for two cables, and 50% for three or more cables; a jam ratio of 1.0 requires downsizing the conduit. Option C. 25% fill regardless of cable count, with no jam risk when pulling three cables around 90-degree sweeps. Option D. 100% fill for fiber-optic cables and 75% fill for Category 6A twisted pair.

clips.label: Question 94
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Magnetic-field vs electric-field EMI shielding materials. Low-level analog microphone lines must pass near high-current mains feeders. Why does wrapping a cable in aluminum foil or copper braid fail to block low-frequency magnetic-field induction, and what should the designer specify instead? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. Non-ferrous metals like aluminum, copper, and brass lack magnetic permeability and block only electric-field (capacitive) coupling; blocking magnetic fields requires physical separation or magnetically permeable steel conduit. Option B. Aluminum foil amplifies 60 Hz magnetic fields by acting as a step-up transformer. Option C. Copper braid blocks magnetic fields only when disconnected from earth ground at both ends. Option D. Plastic PVC cable trays provide 120 dB of magnetic-field attenuation.

clips.label: Question 95
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Earth-leakage protection (GFCI/RCD) nuisance tripping coordination. How does a Residual Current Device (RCD) or Ground-Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI) protect personnel, and why must the AV designer coordinate its selection carefully with the electrical engineer? Choose the single best answer. Option A. It senses any current imbalance between line and neutral (typically 10 to 100 mA) and disconnects within 5 to 100 ms, which can nuisance-trip if several switched-mode supplies or discharge projectors with inherent earth leakage share one device. Option B. It measures the temperature of the rack rails and trips only when current exceeds 200 amperes. Option C. It injects a 1 kHz tone onto the safety ground wire to cancel hum in unbalanced RCA cables. Option D. It disconnects the protective-earth conductor while leaving the hot line energized during a fault.

clips.label: Question 96
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Forward vs reverse phase-control and sine-wave dimmer coordination. When coordinating architectural dimmer specifications with the electrical and lighting engineers for an acoustically sensitive recital hall, which dimmer technology produces the least lamp filament sing and electromagnetic interference on nearby audio wiring? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Sine-wave dimmers using insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) pulse-width modulation, which preserve a smooth sinusoidal waveform rather than chopping the leading or trailing edge. Option B. Forward phase-control leading-edge SCR/triac dimmers that switch abruptly at the peak of the AC cycle. Option C. Unfiltered mechanical rotary rheostats wired in series with the audio mixer. Option D. High-voltage DC arc-discharge ballasts mounted inside the audio rack.

clips.label: Question 97
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Reserve DHCP vs manual static IP assignment for AV devices. An AV control processor must reliably communicate with 15 networked displays and DSPs on a corporate LAN that runs an enterprise DHCP server. What IP addressing method is considered best practice when coordinating with the IT network manager? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Use Reserve DHCP, where the network manager binds a fixed IP address to each AV device's unique 48-bit MAC address in the DHCP server table. Option B. Manually type random static IP addresses from the DHCP pool into each display without telling IT. Option C. Rely on APIPA link-local 169.254.x.x addresses so traffic can route across corporate VLANs. Option D. Use standard dynamic DHCP leases that change every 4 hours without updating the control system.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Specifying background noise with NR/NC or RC curves vs A-weighted dB. ANSI/ASA S12.60 prohibits measuring background noise in learning spaces.

Cubic rooms have zero reverberation time at frequencies above 2 kHz.

clips.label: Question 113
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Integration interval for speech (30 ms) vs music (50 ms) and echo threshold. How does the human ear integrate early reflections for speech versus music, and at what arrival delay do reflections degrade speech intelligibility by sounding like discrete echoes? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Reflections arriving within about 30 ms for speech (or 50 ms for music) integrate with direct sound to add loudness and fullness, whereas reflections arriving 50 to 80 ms or later are heard as discrete echoes that harm intelligibility. Option B. All reflections arriving after 1 ms are perceived as distinct echoes in speech rooms. Option C. Speech requires reflections delayed by 250 ms to be intelligible. Option D. Early reflections within 10 ms completely cancel all direct sound in an auditorium.

clips.label: Question 114
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: STC vs IIC ratings and low-frequency limitation of STC. When coordinating partition ratings with an acoustician for a lecture room located beside a mechanical plant and below a busy lobby, what is the difference between Sound Transmission Class (STC) and Impact Insulation Class (IIC)? Choose the single best answer. Option A. STC rates airborne speech-band isolation (125 Hz to 4 kHz, ignoring low-frequency rumble below 125 Hz), whereas IIC rates structure-borne footfall and impact insulation through floor-ceiling assemblies (100 Hz to 3.15 kHz). Option B. STC measures low-frequency subwoofer isolation from 10 Hz to 100 Hz, whereas IIC measures optical screen contrast. Option C. Both STC and IIC measure interior reverberation decay time (RT60). Option D. STC applies only to outdoor stadiums, whereas IIC applies only to underwater transducers.

clips.label: Question 115

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Porous quarter-wavelength placement vs resonant panel absorbers. Why does mounting a thin porous absorber flush against a rigid wall provide poor low-frequency absorption, and where does a porous absorber work most efficiently? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Acoustic particle velocity is zero right at a rigid boundary and reaches a maximum one-quarter wavelength from the wall; spacing porous material away from the boundary (or using a resonant panel/cavity absorber) improves low-frequency absorption. Option B. Porous absorbers work only when submerged in water. Option C. Sound pressure is zero at a rigid boundary and maximum at the center of the room for all frequencies. Option D. Porous absorbers reflect 100 percent of frequencies above 1 kHz when spaced off a wall.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Axial, tangential, and oblique room modes relative energy. When evaluating standing waves below the Schroeder frequency in a rectangular room, how do axial, tangential, and oblique room modes compare in boundary involvement and relative acoustic energy? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Axial modes reflect between two parallel surfaces and carry the highest energy; tangential modes involve four surfaces (about −3 dB relative to axial); oblique modes involve all six surfaces (about −6 dB relative to axial). Option B. Oblique modes are 10 dB louder than axial modes and involve only the floor. Option C. Tangential modes occur only in spherical domes above 10 kHz. Option D. Axial modes cancel themselves out and require no acoustic treatment.

clips.label: Question 121
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Fire alarm system integration (mute, emergency override, egress). When coordinating a venue's AV system with the fire alarm and life-safety engineer, what automated behavior must occur immediately when the building fire alarm activates? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Mute or interrupt local program audio, allow emergency voice evacuation messages and visual alerts to take precedence, and restore egress lighting and motorized screens/drapes as required by life-safety code. Option B. Boost the main program subwoofer level by 10 dB so the audience hears music over the fire bells. Option C. Lock all motorized projection screens in the down position across exit doors. Option D. Wait 15 minutes for the control processor to finish archiving lecture recordings before muting audio.

clips.label: Question 122
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Return air plenum cable fire rating coordination. Why must the AV designer specify plenum-rated cabling (or metallic conduit) whenever cables are routed through an architectural ceiling space that serves as a return air plenum? Choose the single best answer. Option A. A return air plenum circulates air back to the HVAC handler; non-plenum cable jackets release toxic smoke and accelerate flame spread across the building during a fire, violating AHJ life-safety codes. Option B. Plenum-rated jackets reduce digital video bit error rates by 50 percent. Option C. Non-plenum cables have higher electrical capacitance that blocks 48 V phantom power. Option D. Plenum rating refers solely to the tensile breaking strength of the copper conductors.

clips.label: Question 125
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Fire suppression systems (wet, dry, chemical, hypoxic) in AV rooms. When coordinating fire protection for a mission-critical master control and server room with the fire-safety engineer, what hazard must be noted regarding chemical (CO2/halomethane) and hypoxic fire suppression systems? Choose the single best answer. Option A. While wet and dry water sprinklers damage energized electronics, chemical systems can asphyxiate occupants upon discharge and hypoxic systems maintain reduced oxygen (10% to 14%), requiring strict life-safety protocols. Option B. Wet pipe sprinkler systems use non-conductive deionized gas that is completely harmless to open high-voltage amplifiers. Option C. Hypoxic fire systems increase room oxygen to 45% to cool equipment racks. Option D. Chemical suppression systems require no warning alarms or egress delays before discharging CO2.

segments.text: When coordinating fire protection for a mission-critical master control and server room with the fire-safety engineer, what hazard must be noted regarding chemical (CO2/halomethane) and hypoxic fire suppression systems?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose the single best answer.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. While wet and dry water sprinklers damage energized electronics, chemical systems can asphyxiate occupants upon discharge and hypoxic systems maintain reduced oxygen (10% to 14%), requiring strict life-safety protocols.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Wet pipe sprinkler systems use non-conductive deionized gas that is completely harmless to open high-voltage amplifiers.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. Hypoxic fire systems increase room oxygen to 45% to cool equipment racks.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. Chemical suppression systems require no warning alarms or egress delays before discharging CO2.

clips.label: Question 126
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Atmospheric fog/haze effects and fire detection coordination. A performing arts venue design includes theatrical fog, haze, and pyrotechnic effects. Why must the AV and theatrical designer coordinate these systems directly with the fire-safety engineer? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Airborne particulates and heat from atmospheric or pyrotechnic effects can falsely trigger optical/ionization smoke detectors unless the fire detection zoning and sensor types are engineered for them. Option B. Theatrical fog increases the speed of sound in air by 500 meters per second. Option C. Haze machines automatically silence the building's main fire alarm panel. Option D. Atmospheric effects are regulated solely by the acoustic consultant under ANSI/ASA S12.60.

clips.label: Question 127
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Physical security exposure of displays visible from public lobbies. During a physical security walkthrough of an executive boardroom design, you notice a glass curtain wall allows visitors in the public elevator lobby to see the main videowall clearly. How should the CTS-D address this vulnerability? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Flag the visual eavesdropping risk to physical security stakeholders and coordinate switchable privacy glass, motorized blackout shades, or reoriented display placement. Option B. Ignore the glass wall because network encryption on the HDMI switcher prevents people in the lobby from reading the screen. Option C. Install a firewall ACL on the boardroom router to block optical light waves through the glass. Option D. Lower the videowall brightness to 5 cd/m² so neither the board members nor lobby visitors can see it.

clips.label: Question 129
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and life-safety compliance sequence. Put the steps for ensuring life-safety, fire-code, and regulatory compliance across an AV design in the proper professional order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Identify the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and gather all applicable national, regional, and local building, electrical, fire, and accessibility codes. Step 2: Compare overlapping codes and standards and adopt the most stringent requirement wherever interpretations conflict. Step 3: Integrate life-safety interfaces (fire alarm mute/override, plenum ratings, sprinkler clearances, ADA reach/protrusion limits) into the AV design drawings and specifications. Step 4: Verify and document life-safety and regulatory compliance with the AHJ and allied professionals before final sign-off.

clips.label: Question 130
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Air-gapped AV network physical and wireless isolation. A defense contractor requires an 'air-gapped' AV network for a classified command center. What must the AV designer ensure when coordinating with physical and network security officials? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The AV network must have zero physical or wireless connections to enterprise infrastructure or external networks, with locked physical enclosures and tamper protection. Option B. The AV network may share the corporate core switch provided it uses a different IPv4 subnet mask. Option C. The command center processors should connect to the Internet only at night for automatic cloud firmware updates. Option D. Air-gapping means mounting the network switches at least 2 meters above the rack floor.

clips.label: Question 134
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Estimating activity duration vs optimistic effort in construction schedules. Why must an AV designer and project manager provide 'duration' estimates rather than raw 'effort' estimates when merging the AV schedule into the general contractor's master Gantt chart? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Effort is only the active labor time on task (often estimated optimistically), whereas duration is the actual elapsed calendar time accounting for work periods, travel, logistics, predecessor waits, and resource availability across projects. Option B. Duration is always shorter than effort because technicians work 24 hours a day. Option C. General contractors schedule trades using decibel ratios rather than calendar days. Option D. Effort includes shipping delays and concrete curing time, whereas duration ignores them.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Custom lectern and millwork drawings for cabinetmakers. A courtroom project requires custom wooden witness stands and a judge's bench housing integrated microphones, confidence monitors, and touch panels. How must the AV designer coordinate with the millwork artisan? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Include detailed custom furniture dimensions, cut-out tolerances, ventilation paths, cable access, and ergonomic sightline/reach drawings in the AV design package so the cabinetmaker builds to exact requirements. clips.label: Question 140
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Performance standards vs technical standards in trade coordination. When explaining AV standards to project-specific consultants, what is the fundamental distinction between a 'performance standard' (such as ANSI/AVIXA V201.01 ISCR) and a 'technical standard'? Choose the single best answer. Option A. A performance standard ensures the complete installed system operates as intended and meets user outcome metrics, whereas a technical standard defines product characteristics so devices interoperate. Option B. A performance standard applies only to theatrical stage actors, whereas a technical standard applies only to hand tools. Option C. Performance standards mandate a single equipment brand, whereas technical standards have no measurable values. Option D. Technical standards are legally binding statutes in every country, whereas performance standards prohibit field testing.

clips.label: Question 146
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Conceptual projection and display design sequence. Order the steps for developing a conceptual projection display design from content classification through projector lens positioning. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Classify the primary viewing category (Passive, BDM, ADM, or Full-Motion Video) based on the detail viewers must resolve. Step 2: Apply DISCAS and a 30-degree sightline study to determine required image height, viewing cone, and nearest/farthest viewer distances. Step 3: Calculate required projector lumens from ambient light at the screen, ISCR minimum contrast ratio, screen area, screen gain, and the 0.75 derating factor. Step 4: Select the projector and lens throw ratio to establish the throw distance and horizontal/vertical offsets.

clips.label: Question 149
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Screen gain trade-off: narrowing viewing cone and hot spotting. When creating a conceptual projection design for a wide-seating lecture room, what trade-off occurs if the designer selects a high-gain front-projection screen (e.g., gain > 1.5) instead of a unity-gain (1.0) matte white screen? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. A high-gain screen redistributes light into a narrower on-axis viewing cone—reducing brightness for off-axis viewers and increasing the risk of visible hot spotting. Option B. A high-gain screen actively generates extra photons and widens the horizontal viewing angle to 180 degrees. Option C. A unity-gain (1.0) screen absorbs 90 percent of the projector's light output. Option D. Screen gain affects only the correlated color temperature of room task lighting.

Not this one: The choice "A unity-gain (1.0) screen absorbs 90…light output" uses the wrong value, unit, or relationship for the stated quantities. Decisive rule: Screens do not amplify light; a gain above 1.0 concentrates reflected light toward the on-axis viewer at the expense of off-axis seating angles and can cause uneven bright centers (hot spotting). Best answer: A high-gain screen redistributes light into a narrower on-axis viewing cone—reducing brightness for off-axis viewers and increasing the risk of visible hot spotting.

clips.label: Question 150
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Diffusion vs optical two-lens rear-projection screens. How does a two-element optical rear-projection screen differ in construction and performance from a simple diffusion rear-projection screen? Choose the single best answer. Option A. An optical rear screen combines a Fresnel lens (facing the projector to collimate light) with a vertical lenticular lens (facing the audience to control horizontal dispersion and reject ambient light), whereas a diffusion screen scatters light broadly with little or no gain. Option B. A diffusion screen uses two polarized mirrors that block all off-axis viewing beyond 10 degrees. Option C. An optical rear screen must be mounted with the Fresnel grooves facing the audience and the lenticular ribs facing the projector. Option D. Diffusion rear screens cannot be fabricated from rigid acrylic or glass.

clips.label: Question 151
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Distributed ceiling loudspeaker spacing configurations and dB variation. When laying out a conceptual distributed ceiling loudspeaker grid using coverage radius r, how do the three standard spacing configurations—edge-to-edge (2r), partial overlap (r × 1.41 square), and edge-to-center (r)—compare in SPL uniformity? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Edge-to-edge (2r) has ~4.35 dB variation in a square grid; partial ~20% overlap (r × 1.41 square or r × 1.73 hex) yields ~3 dB variation; edge-to-center 50% overlap (r) yields ~1.4 dB variation. Option B. Edge-to-edge (2r) provides 0 dB variation, whereas edge-to-center (r) creates a 12 dB drop between speakers. Option C. All distributed ceiling layouts must space loudspeakers exactly 10 meters apart regardless of ceiling height. Option D. Hexagonal edge-to-edge spacing eliminates all uncovered gaps at 20 kHz.

clips.label: Question 152
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Three-to-one (3:1) microphone placement rule to minimize comb filtering. In a conceptual audio design for a panel discussion table with multiple active gooseneck microphones, how does the 3:1 rule govern microphone spacing? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. The distance between any two adjacent microphones should be at least three times the distance from each talker to their own microphone, attenuating off-axis pickup by ~10 dB and minimizing phase comb filtering. Option B. Three microphones must be wired in series for every one preamplifier channel. Option C. The talker must sit three times farther from the microphone than the ceiling loudspeaker height. Option D. Every third microphone must have its XLR pin 2 and pin 3 polarity reversed.

clips.label: Question 153
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Number of Open Microphones (NOM) 3 dB penalty per doubling. How does doubling the Number of Open Microphones (NOM) in a sound reinforcement system affect the system's potential acoustic gain before feedback, and how does an automatic mixer help? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Each doubling of open microphones reduces gain before feedback by 3 dB (10 × log NOM); an automatic mixer uses gated or gain sharing to keep the effective NOM near one. Option B. Each doubling of open microphones increases potential acoustic gain by 6 dB. Option C. Opening eight microphones reduces gain before feedback by 24 dB (20 × log NOM). Option D. Automatic mixers eliminate the need to place loudspeakers away from microphones.

clips.label: Question 154
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Direct-connected loudspeaker amplifier sizing workflow. Order the four steps for specifying the required power amplifier output for a directly connected (low-impedance) loudspeaker system. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Determine the target average Sound Pressure Level (Lp) required at the farthest listener distance (D2). Step 2: Add the appropriate program headroom allowance (H = 10 dB for speech or 20 dB for music). Step 3: Calculate the Electrical Power Required (EPR) using the loudspeaker's 1 W / 1 m sensitivity (Ls) and inverse-square distance loss 20 × log(D2 ÷ Dr). Step 4: Round the calculated wattage up to a commercially available power amplifier rating at the circuit's nominal impedance.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Unity-gain vs system-optimization gain structure methods. When designing the conceptual audio signal chain, how should the CTS-D choose between the 'unity-gain method' and the 'system-optimization method' for setting gain structure? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Use the unity-gain method (output = input at each stage, yielding ~60 dB electronic S/N) for typical presentation and conference rooms, and reserve the system-optimization method (uniform headroom and maximum S/N) for critical listening venues like studios, broadcast, and concert halls. Option B. Use the unity-gain method only for passive 70 V loudspeakers and the optimization method only for 4-ohm subwoofers. Option C. Set all microphone preamplifiers to minimum gain and make up +60 dB at the power amplifier inputs. Option D. The system-optimization method requires clipping every analog mixer stage at +28 dBu continuously.

clips.label: Question 165
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Unicast vs multicast streaming architecture selection. A campus design must deliver a single 300 kbps live morning announcement stream simultaneously to 100 classrooms over a legacy 100 Mbps LAN (where the 20% streaming budget equals 20 Mbps). Should the designer specify unicast or multicast, and why? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Specify multicast, because 100 unicast streams would consume 30 Mbps (exceeding the 20 Mbps streaming budget), whereas multicast transmits a single 300 kbps stream replicated by switches/routers. Option B. Specify TCP unicast, because 100 streams of 300 kbps equal only 300 kbps total in unicast mode. Option C. Specify multicast over the public Internet so students can pause and rewind the live stream individually. Option D. Use APIPA 169.254.x.x addressing to route unicast streams across ten routers.

clips.label: Question 171
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: PAG and NAG acoustic stability verification workflow. Sequence the steps for performing the mathematical acoustic stability test (confirming NAG < PAG) on a speech reinforcement design. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Measure or extract from drawings the key distances: talker to farthest listener (D0), mic to nearest speaker (D1), farthest listener to nearest speaker (D2), talker to mic (Ds), and Equivalent Acoustic Distance (EAD). Step 2: Calculate Needed Acoustic Gain: NAG = 20 × log10(D0 ÷ EAD). Step 3: Calculate raw Potential Acoustic Gain: PAG = 20 × log10[(D0 × D1) ÷ (D2 × Ds)]. Step 4: Subtract 10 × log10(NOM) for open microphones and the 6 dB Feedback Stability Margin (FSM) from PAG, and verify that NAG is less than the adjusted PAG.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Digital video interface selection: SDI vs HDMI 2.1 vs HDBaseT vs DisplayPort. When selecting digital video transport interfaces for a conceptual design, how do 3G/12G-SDI, HDMI 2.1a, and HDBaseT (IEEE 1911) differ in reach, connectors, and copy protection? Choose the single best answer. Option A. SDI runs uncompressed, unencrypted broadcast video with time code up to ~100 m over 75-ohm coax with locking BNC connectors (and does not support HDCP); HDMI 2.1a carries up to 48 Gbps with HDCP over short point-to-point runs; HDBaseT extends HDMI, audio, control, Ethernet, and up to 100 Wpower up to 100 m over a single Cat 5e/6 cable. Option B. SDI carries HDCP 2.2 encrypted consumer Blu-ray movies over RJ-45 connectors up to 500 m. Option C. Digital DVI-D natively carries 32 channels of embedded audio, CEC control, and 100 W PoE. Option D. HDBaseT is limited to 2 meters over multimode optical fiber.

clips.label: Question 174
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Verifying printed drawing scale against a known element ('fit to page' trap). Before measuring room dimensions off a printed architectural floor plan to revise a conceptual AV layout, why must the designer check the drawing scale against a known dimension such as a standard door opening or ceiling tile? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Printer drivers set to 'fit to page' rescale the drawing and invalidate every ruler measurement unless verified against a known reference element. Option B. Architectural scales change automatically depending on the room's relative humidity. Option C. Metric 1:100 drawings cannot be printed on paper larger than A4. Option D. Checking a door width tells the designer the room's reverberation time (RT60).

clips.label: Question 177
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Revising microphone preamp selection using the dBu mic output formula. Site conditions require a presenter to stand 600 mm from a podium microphone producing 72 dB SPL (22 dB below the 94 dB SPL / 1 Pa reference). Using Mic Output (dBu) = SPL_measured − SPL_ref + Sensitivity (dBV/Pa) + 2.21, why must a conceptual mic with −54.5 dBV/Pa sensitivity be replaced if the mixer preamp provides at most 60 dB of gain to reach 0 dBu? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The −54.5 dBV/Pa mic outputs −74.29 dBu (72 − 94 − 54.5 + 2.21), requiring 74.29 dB of preamp gain to reach 0 dBu—exceeding the preamp's 60 dB limit by ~14.3 dB; selecting a higher-sensitivity mic (such as −35 dBV/Pa, outputting −54.79 dBu) fits within the 60 dB preamp range. Option B. A −54.5 dBV/Pa microphone outputs +54.5 V DC and will overload the mixer input. Option C. The 2.21 constant converts ohms into watts on constant-voltage speaker lines. Option D. Lowering preamp gain to 10 dB and boosting power amplifier gain by 65 dB solves the shortfall without noise.

clips.label: Question 178
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Fixed-microphone feedback-suppression filter procedure. Order the four steps of the Chapter 14 procedure for setting narrow input notch filters to suppress acoustic feedback on a fixed microphone before final room equalization. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Mute all other microphones in the room so only the fixed test microphone is active. Step 2: Slowly raise gain on the test microphone and note the first three frequencies that begin to feed back. Step 3: Build three tight-notch (high-Q) parametric filters at those exact frequencies on that microphone's input channel. Step 4: Reset the gain, equalize the overall sound system, then re-engage the notch filters and verify stable operational level.

A higher f-stop number doubles the lumen output of the projector. Option C. Changing lenses affects only the image aspect ratio and has zero effect on brightness. Option D. Optical zoom lenses regenerate digital pixels via active reclocking.

clips.label: Question 181
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Revising ceiling loudspeaker placement away from conference table head and walls. When revising a reflected ceiling plan after the interior designer rotates the boardroom table, you notice a ceiling loudspeaker now sits directly above the head of the table where the presenter's lectern microphone is placed, and another sits within 300 mm of a hard glass wall. What design revision is required? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Relocate or zone off the loudspeaker directly above the presenter microphone to preserve PAG/feedback stability, and keep loudspeaker coverage patterns off adjacent hard walls to prevent early reflections. Option B. Increase the transformer tap wattage on the loudspeaker directly over the presenter's microphone. Option C. Aim all ceiling loudspeakers directly at the glass wall to increase reverberation. Option D. Wire an omnidirectional microphone directly underneath the HVAC supply diffuser instead.

clips.label: Question 185
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Active reclocking vs passive balun extenders for site pathway lengths. A revised conduit routing plan increases the cable run between a lectern HDMI source and the rack switcher from 30 m to 85 m over Category 6A cable. Why must the designer revise a passive balun extender to an active twisted-pair or fiber extender? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Passive balun extenders do not reclock or regenerate the digital signal and are limited to roughly 50 m (165 ft), whereas active wired extenders reclock and regenerate the signal up to 100 m (330 ft) and fiber extenders reach up to 30 km. Option B. Passive baluns require 480 V AC power at both ends and only work up to 2 meters. Option C. Active extenders strip HDCP encryption so signals can travel over unshielded speaker wire. Option D. Passive extenders from different manufacturers can be mixed at either end to double the distance.

clips.label: Question 186
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Adjusting delay speaker settings for site air temperature and altitude. When revising DSP delay calculations for an outdoor amphitheater located in a hot desert climate (30 °C / 86 °F) versus a standard 20 °C (68 °F) indoor room, how does the speed of sound change? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The speed of sound increases with air temperature—from about 343 m/s at 20 °C to about 350 m/s at 30 °C—and also varies with altitude, requiring delay times to be adjusted accordingly. Option B. The speed of sound drops to 150 m/s in warm air. Option C. Air temperature affects only optical fiber latency and has zero effect on acoustic waves. Option D. Sound travels instantaneously in outdoor venues above 25 °C.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Parametric EQ vs graphic EQ for solving narrow room resonances. Site acoustic testing reveals two narrow resonant frequency peaks in a lecture room. Graphic equalizers eliminate the Schroeder frequency in cubic rooms.

clips.label: Question 192
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: A&E drawing review and conceptual design revision workflow. Order the steps for reviewing an updated Architectural & Engineering (A&E) drawing package and revising the conceptual AV design to match site conditions. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Verify the drawing scale against a known architectural dimension and confirm consistent measurement units across all imported CAD files. Step 2: Cross-check plan views, reflected ceiling plans, elevations, and building sections for structural, HVAC, lighting, sprinkler, and millwork clashes. Step 3: Recalculate affected AV parameters—including sightlines, throw distances, loudspeaker coverage, conduit fill, branch-circuit loads, and heat dissipation. Step 4: Update the AV drawings, specifications, and allied-trade coordination notes and obtain stakeholder sign-off on the revised design.

Standing inside the projector beam increases the screen's ISCR contrast ratio to 80:1.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Resolving ground-loop hum via shield integrity and balanced/isolated design. During a site retrofit review, existing analog audio tie-lines between a stage box and a control booth on different branch circuits exhibit 60 Hz hum. What is the most common root cause and proper engineering fix? Choose the single best answer. Option A. clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Acoustic diffuser surface irregularity and wavelength sizing. While revising room acoustic treatment with the acoustician to eliminate flutter echoes without making the room dead, what physical dimension rule determines whether a geometric wall diffuser will effectively scatter a given sound wavelength? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Surface irregularity depths/widths must be comparable to the sound wavelength being diffused, and the overall diffuser surface must be at least one wavelength wide (and up to roughly four wavelengths). Option B. A 2 mm textured wallpaper scatters 100 Hz low-frequency standing waves completely. Option C. Diffusers absorb 100 percent of incident acoustic energy like an open 1-sabin window. Option D. Diffusers work only when mounted flush behind heavy velvet curtains.

segments.text: During a site revision, an installer proposes inserting a passive non-isolated in-line attenuator pad on a balanced microphone line that carries 48 V DC phantom power to a condenser gooseneck mic. Why must the designer reject or carefully specify this pad?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose the single best answer.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. Many in-line attenuator pads block DC phantom power or can be damaged by 48 V DC on the signal conductors; adjust preamp input gain/pad settings or use a phantom-power-compatible circuit instead.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Phantom power travels only on Pin 1 (shield) and never touches the two signal conductors.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. 48 V phantom power melts balanced dynamic microphone voice coils immediately upon connection.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. Attenuator pads boost condenser microphone sensitivity by +20 dB.

clips.label: Question 203
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: ANSI-J-STD-710 architectural AV drawing symbol standard and legend. Which joint industry standard defines architectural floor plan and reflected ceiling plan symbols for audio, video, and control devices, and what must every drawing sheet include so trades interpret those symbols accurately? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. ANSI-J-STD-710 (developed jointly by AVIXA, CTA/CEA, and CEDIA); every drawing package must include a symbol legend or key defining each symbol used. Option B. IEEE 802.11ax; symbols are interpreted without a legend by measuring line thickness. Option C. ANSI/ASA S12.60; symbols apply only to structural steel welds. Option D. ITU-R BT.1359; symbols are proprietary to each CAD operator.

clips.label: Question 208
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Signal separation in rack design (50,000:1 / ~94 dB ratio between mic and mains). Why do ANSI/AVIXA F502.01 and F502.02 require strict physical separation between microphone-level signal cables and AC mains power cables inside an equipment rack? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Microphone signals (~1 to 10 mV) and AC mains power (100 to 240 V) differ in voltage by roughly 50,000:1, so routing them together induces severe electromagnetic hum and noise into the audio path. Option B. Microphone cables carry 100 A of DC current that overheats AC power cords. Option C. Separating cables increases the rack's total weight in the top third. Option D. AC power cables attenuate optical fiber light pulses via capacitive reactance.

clips.label: Question 209
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Ergonomic rack elevation placement of interactive vs non-interactive gear. When laying out a final rack elevation drawing, where should interactive user-operated devices (such as optical disc players, media decks, and local control panels) be positioned relative to non-interactive devices (such as wireless mic receivers and patch panels)? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Place interactive devices in the ergonomic zone between seated and standing user eye height, heavy gear (UPS, amps) in the bottom third, and non-interactive/high-heat gear near the top or bottom. Option B. Place user disc players at floor level (1 RU) and heavy UPS battery banks at the very top (48 RU). Option C. Mount wireless microphone receivers inside a sealed steel drawer at the bottom of the rack. Option D. Place adjacent devices with opposite front-to-back and back-to-front cooling fans directly on top of each other without blanking panels.

clips.label: Question 215
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Common-Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR) and transformer-balanced audio specification. Why does a final audio specification call for differential balanced inputs with high Common-Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR, typically 70 to 120 dB) or transformer-balanced isolation on long cable runs? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Two identical twisted conductors carry opposite-polarity signals while external noise couples equally into both; the differential receiver inverts and sums the signals, canceling common-mode noise while doubling the desired signal. Option B. Balanced circuits carry mains power on Pin 2 and loudspeaker output on Pin 3. Option C. CMRR amplifies 60 Hz hum by 120 dB so it masks background HVAC noise. Option D. Unbalanced coaxial cables have higher common-mode rejection than transformer-balanced twisted pair.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: DisplayPort 2.0, USB4, and Thunderbolt 3/4 Type-C capabilities on lectern plates. When designing a modern lectern connectivity plate, how do DisplayPort 2.0, Thunderbolt 3/4, and USB4 over USB Type-C connectors compare in bandwidth and tunneling capabilities? Option B. USB Type-C connectors can carry only 480 Mbps USB 2.0 keyboard data and cannot carry video. Option C. Thunderbolt 4 runs up to 100 meters over unshielded Category 3 telephone wire. Option D. DisplayPort 2.0 uses a 3-pin XLR connector and carries no HDCP encryption.

clips.label: Question 230
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Ohm's law and power equation two-step derivation for loudspeaker loads. While checking a final circuit specification where a 4 V test signal dissipates 2 Wof power in a load, how do you derive the load's resistance in ohms using the power equation (P = I × V) and Ohm's law (I = V ÷ R)? Choose the single best answer. Option A. First solve for current using the power equation: I = P ÷ V = 2 W ÷ 4 V = 0.5 A; then apply Ohm's law: R = V ÷ I = 4 V ÷ 0.5 A = 8 ohms. Option B. Multiply voltage by power: R = 4 V × 2 W = 80 ohms. Option C. Divide power by voltage squared: R = 2 ÷ 16 = 0.125 ohms. Option D. Add voltage and power: R = 4 + 2 = 6 ohms.

clips.label: Question 235
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Risk Register fields and four risk response strategies in final security docs. When finalizing the Networked AV Security Risk Register before design sign-off, which four risk response strategies can be assigned to each identified vulnerability, and what four elements must every 'Mitigate' entry include? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The four responses are Avoid, Accept, Transfer, and Mitigate; every mitigation plan must specify a concrete action, a contingency plan, a responsible party (owner), and a due date. Option B. The four responses are Ignore, Conceal, Delay, and Blame; no owner or due date is recorded. Option C. The four responses are Compress, Equalize, Limit, and Gate. Option D. Transferring a risk means deleting the vulnerability from the register without insurance or cloud service agreements.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Decibel power (10 log) vs voltage/distance (20 log) formulas in design docs. When finalizing audio and RF link budgets in project documentation, when must the designer use the 10 × log10(P1 ÷ P2) formula versus the 20 × log10(V1 ÷ V2) or 20 × log10(D1 ÷ D2) formula? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Use 10 × log10 for power quantities (watts, dBW, dBm), and use 20 × log10 for voltage, current, sound pressure level (SPL), or inverse-square distance ratios (so doubling power is +3 dB, whereas doubling voltage or halving distance is +6 dB). Option B. Use 20 × log10 for amplifier wattage and 10 × log10 for loudspeaker throw distance. Option C. Doubling amplifier wattage increases output by +10 dB, and doubling distance increases SPL by +20 dB. Option D. A negative decibel value (−50 dBu) indicates a negative polarity DC voltage.

Noise gates are placed after the loudspeaker crossover to boost subwoofer output.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Whiteboard reflectance specification (40-60% gray) in camera rooms. A bright, high-reflectance glossy whiteboard causes specular hot spots and tricks camera auto-iris into darkening the presenter's face, whereas a 40–60% reflectance matte/low-gloss gray board preserves facial exposure balance. Option B. Cameras cannot focus on gray surfaces at distances greater than 2 meters. Option C. A 100% glossy whiteboard doubles the acoustic absorption of the front wall. Option D. Gray markerboards can also be used as 15:1 contrast front-projection screens without hot spotting.

clips.label: Question 257
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Gated sharing vs gain sharing automatic microphone mixer specification. When finalizing the DSP specification for a 24-microphone boardroom, how does a 'gain-sharing' automatic mixer differ operationally from a 'gated-sharing' automatic mixer? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Gated sharing switches channels on/off above a set threshold (which can clip initial syllables or sound choppy if thresholds are misadjusted), whereas gain sharing continuously proportions total system gain across channels based on relative voice activity for smoother transitions. Option B. Gain sharing turns all 24 microphones to maximum gain simultaneously so NOM equals 24. Option C. Gated sharing requires a human operator to manually unmute every syllable. Option D. Neither automatic mixing method controls the Number of Open Microphones (NOM).

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: HDCP four-step authentication and source-to-sink fault isolation. During commissioning, a protected video source displays a black screen or snow due to an HDCP authentication failure. What are the four steps of HDCP authentication, and how should the fault be isolated in the field? Choose the single best answer. Option A. HDCP executes (1) device authentication/key exchange, (2) locality check, (3) session key exchange, and (4) repeater authentication; isolate the fault by starting at the source end with a known-working display and testing point-by-point along the path. Option B. HDCP authentication runs only once at factory manufacture; isolate faults by replacing the room's acoustic ceiling tiles. Option C. Start troubleshooting at the farthest display with an untested cable and work backward without a test monitor. Option D. HDCP passes unencrypted content during step 1 before repeater authentication completes.

clips.label: Question 264
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Resolving lip-sync errors across multiple displays with different processing delays. During systems integration in an auditorium with both a low-latency stage monitor and a heavily processed videowall, presenters notice audio and video are out of sync. Why can't HDMI EDID auto-lip-sync alone solve this, and what is the proper fix? Choose the single best answer. Option A. HDMI EDID lip-sync compensation can align audio to only one display's latency; when multiple displays have different video processing delays, manual electronic delay must be added via the audio DSP or per-output delay stages so the less-delayed signals match the most-delayed display. Option B. Speed up the videowall processor beyond the speed of light using an EDID emulator. Option C. Move the loudspeakers 50 meters farther away from the audience. Option D. Switch the audio sampling rate from 48 kHz to 8 kHz to advance the audio in time.

clips.label: Question 265
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Troubleshooting broadband hiss caused by low preamp gain and high amp gain. During commissioning, a conference room sound system produces loud constant hiss from the loudspeakers even when nobody is speaking. Checking the rack reveals the microphone preamplifiers are set very low (−30 dBu) while the power amplifiers and output stages are turned to maximum gain. What is the cause and correction? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Low gain at the early preamplifier stage forced downstream stages to amplify the electronic noise floor; set the microphone preamps properly to bring the signal to nominal line level (0 dBu / +4 dBu) early in the chain and reduce excess downstream gain. Option B. Insert a graphic equalizer after the power amplifier to boost 10 kHz by +15 dB. Option C. Replace the balanced XLR microphone cables with unshielded speaker wire. Option D. Lower the microphone preamp gain another 20 dB.

clips.label: Question 266
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Correcting camera backlight overexposure by balancing room lighting vs BLC. During camera commissioning in a boardroom with an exterior window, participants appear as dark silhouettes. The installer turns on the camera's digital Backlight Compensation (BLC), which blows out the background into blinding white glare. What should the CTS-D direct the team to do? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. Treat BLC as only a temporary workaround; properly balance the room's optical lighting by closing/filtering window treatments and raising key/fill illuminance on the participants relative to the background wash. Option B. Leave BLC enabled and mount a 1,000 Wfloodlight on the window pointing straight into the camera lens. Option C. Switch the camera from progressive scan to interlaced scan to fix the window glare. Option D. Defocus the camera lens so the blown-out background is blurred.

clips.label: Question 269
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Understanding ICT (Image Constraint Token) and DOT (Digital-Only Token) flags. During system integration testing of a media server, a high-definition source suddenly down-resolutions its output or displays an on-screen warning when routed through a legacy analog component output or improperly authenticated repeater. clips.label: Question 270
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Checking rack thermal gradient and opposing fan airflow during integration. During systems integration verification of a populated equipment rack, you find a video processor running dangerously hot because the device mounted immediately below it exhausts hot air out its front panel while the processor draws cooling intake air from its front panel. What should be done? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Re-space or reorder the rack layout and install blanking or vented directional panels so devices with opposite airflow directions do not short-circuit hot exhaust air into adjacent cooling intakes. Option B. Seal all rack vents with duct tape so no air can move inside the enclosure. Option C. Remove the video processor's outer chassis cover and leave its live power supply exposed. Option D. Move the heavy UPS battery bank from the bottom of the rack to the top RU.

Option B. Measure at a single point 100 mm in front of the projector lens with an incident lux meter. Option C. Average all five positions together so a 30:1 reading in the front row excuses a 4:1 reading in the back row. Option D. Measure contrast with all room task and ambient lights turned completely off in a room designed for daylight note-taking.

clips.label: Question 274
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Nine-zone ANSI lumens field verification formula. To verify a projector's actual light output in the field using the ANSI nine-zone method, you divide the screen into a 3×3 grid of nine equal rectangles, measure the incident illuminance (Z1 through Z9) at the center of each zone in lux, and measure screen height (SH) and width (SW) in meters. Which formula gives ANSI lumens? Choose the single best answer. Option A. ANSI Lumens = [(Z1 + Z2 + Z3 + Z4 + Z5 + Z6 + Z7 + Z8 + Z9) ÷ 9] × (SH × SW). Option B. ANSI Lumens = (Z1 × Z9) ÷ (SH + SW). Option C. ANSI Lumens = [(Z1 + … + Z9) × 9] ÷ (SH × SW). Option D. ANSI Lumens = Center Zone Z5 × Throw Distance.

Option B. Class 2 meters are more accurate (±0.01 dB) than Class 1 meters (±10 dB). Option C. Uncalibrated smartphone microphones automatically meet IEC 61672 Class 1 certification. Option D. Class 1 SPL meters measure only optical luminance in candelas per square meter.

clips.label: Question 276
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: SPL frequency weightings: A-weighting vs C-weighting vs Z-weighting. When configuring a classified sound level meter for system performance verification, how do A-weighting, C-weighting, and Z-weighting differ in frequency response and application? Choose the single best answer. Option A. A-weighting filters low frequencies to approximate human ear sensitivity at lower levels (used for speech and background noise like 35 dBA); C-weighting is much flatter with −3 dB points at 31.5 Hz and 8 kHz (used for high listening levels of 85–140 dB SPL); Z-weighting is unweighted flat response (±1.5 dB from 10 Hz to 20 kHz). Option B. A-weighting is completely flat from 1 Hz to 100 kHz, while Z-weighting rolls off 40 dB at 100 Hz. Option C. C-weighting measures only frequencies between 1 kHz and 2 kHz. Option D. Weighting filters need not be noted on verification reports because all three give identical readings.

clips.label: Question 277
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Audio/video lip-sync tolerances (+40/-60 ms default vs +15/-45 ms television). When performing a 'blip-and-flash' audio/video synchronization verification test (one full-white video frame paired with a matching audio tone), what are the acceptable sync tolerance windows for general AV systems versus broadcast television applications? Choose the single best answer. Option A. For general AV chains (absent specific project criteria), audio may lead video by up to 40 ms or lag video by up to 60 ms; for television applications (per ITU-R BT.1359-1 / EBU R37 / ATSC IS-19), audio may lead by up to 15 ms or lag by up to 45 ms. Option B. Audio may lead video by up to 500 ms and lag by up to 10 ms in broadcast studios. Option C. Human viewers cannot detect lip-sync errors smaller than 2 full seconds. Option D. Audio must always arrive at least 100 ms ahead of video because light travels faster than sound.

Option B. Digital audio signals gain 20 dB of analog warmth when driven to +6 dBFS. Option C. Setting nominal level at −20 dBFS reduces a 24-bit converter to 4-bit resolution. Option D. 0 dBFS represents complete silence in digital audio.

clips.label: Final Cram question 17
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Lamp vs luminaire terminology and luminous efficacy (lm/W). When writing lighting coordination specifications for the architectural team, what is the standard distinction between a 'lamp' and a 'luminaire,' and what does 'efficacy' measure? Choose the single best answer. Option A. A lamp is the light-producing element (bulb, tube, or LED chip array), whereas a luminaire is the complete lighting instrument (lamp, optics, housing, mount, power supply, and control); efficacy measures energy efficiency in lumens per watt (initial lumens ÷ nominal power). Option B. A luminaire is the replaceable glass bulb, and a lamp is the ceiling mounting clamp; efficacy measures color rendering from 0 to 100. Option C. Efficacy is the correlated color temperature measured in degrees Celsius. Option D. A lamp and a luminaire both refer exclusively to 19-inch equipment racks.

clips.label: Final Cram question 18
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Direct glare vs indirect glare (veiling reflections) in display spaces. During an interior coordination review for a boardroom with large windows and a polished marble table, how should the CTS-D distinguish 'direct glare' from 'indirect glare' (veiling reflections)? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Direct glare occurs only at night, while indirect glare occurs only at noon. Option B. Direct glare is bright light from a luminaire or window entering the viewer's eyes or camera lens directly, whereas indirect glare (veiling reflection) is bright light reflected off a glossy surface (like a polished table or glass bezel) into the eyes or lens. Option C. Indirect glare increases the Image System Contrast Ratio (ISCR) to 100:1. Option D. Direct glare is an acoustic reflection arriving after 50 milliseconds.

clips.label: Final Cram question 20
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Structural fastener failure modes: shear, tension, pull-out, and improper load math. When reviewing overhead and wall mounting designs with a structural engineer, what is the difference between 'shearing' failure, 'tensile' failure, and 'pull-out' failure of a mounting fastener? Choose the single best answer. Option A. All three terms mean the paint on the bracket peeled off. Option B. Shearing is corrosion from humidity, tensile is electrical arcing, and pull-out is software crashing. Option C. Shearing is the bolt unscrewing due to vibration, while pull-out is the display glass cracking. Option D. Shearing occurs when weight acts perpendicular across the bolt shaft slicing it; tensile failure occurs when axial load stretches, twists, or snaps the fastener; pull-out occurs when the anchor or bolt tears out of the wall or ceiling substrate.

Choose the single best answer. Option A. It completely disconnects all equipment chassis from earth ground so fault current has no return path. Option B. Option C. It wires the green safety-ground conductor directly to the 208 V hot phase. Option D. It replaces copper branch circuits with unshielded plastic water pipes.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Conservation of acoustic energy at a boundary (reflection, absorption, transmission). When sound energy strikes an interior partition wall, which three physical outcomes occur, and why can't electronic equalization 'fix' a highly reverberant or poorly isolated room? Option B. All sound striking a wall is destroyed by destructive interference. Option C. Graphic equalization absorbs reverberant decay tails inside the air volume. Option D. High absorption coefficients on carpet block 100 Hz subwoofer transmission through walls.
